hints: Look first for what is missing in the high wavenumber region, as O-H and N-H give very distinctive broad absorptions.
Notice the very strong, sharp dip at about 1710 cm-1 and recall which bond always absorbs strongly there.
Combine the presence of that carbonyl peak with the absence of any broad alcohol or acid O-H to narrow Q down to one functional group type.
walkthrough:
**Check for O-H above 3000 cm-1**

Think like a detective and look for the broad O-H hump first. Alcohols show a broad peak at 3200-3600 cm-1 and carboxylic acids show a very broad peak at 2500-3000 cm-1.

Here the baseline near 3500 cm-1 is almost flat, with only a tiny wobble, and the peaks near 3000 cm-1 are sharp. That tells us there is no alcohol O-H and no acid O-H.

**Identify the strong carbonyl peak**

Now focus on the fingerprint workhorse region. A very strong, sharp absorption at about 1700-1750 cm-1 is characteristic of $C=O$ stretching.

$$\text{peak at } \approx 1715 \text{ cm}^{-1} = C=O \text{ stretch}$$

This spectrum has one dominant sharp dip at about 1715 cm-1, so Q definitely contains a carbonyl group.

**Match to the four candidates**

Put the two clues together: C=O present, O-H absent. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ needs O-H, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$ needs C=O plus broad acid O-H, and $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CHO}$ needs both C=O and alcohol O-H.

Only $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$, a ketone with C=O and no O-H, fits perfectly.

options.A: Butan-1-ol, CH3CH2CH2CH2OH, must show a strong broad O-H stretch at 3200-3600 cm-1. The spectrum is essentially flat there, so this is ruled out. The sharp peaks near 2950 cm-1 are just C-H stretches.
options.B: Butanoic acid, CH3CH2CH2COOH, would show C=O near 1710 cm-1 but also a very broad O-H stretch from 2500-3000 cm-1 that overlaps and broadens the C-H region. This spectrum shows sharp C-H peaks and no broad acid hump, so it cannot be a carboxylic acid.
options.C: Butanone, CH3COCH2CH3, is a ketone. It gives C-H stretches just below 3000 cm-1 and a strong sharp C=O stretch at about 1715 cm-1, with no broad O-H absorption above 3000 cm-1. That matches the observed spectrum exactly.
options.D: 3-hydroxybutanal, CH3CH(OH)CH2CHO, contains both an aldehyde C=O and an alcohol O-H. It would therefore show both the 1710 cm-1 carbonyl peak and a broad O-H peak at 3200-3600 cm-1. The missing O-H peak rules it out.
